GRAMMAR can / be able to

Quick rule. Use can for present ability: I can swim. Use be able to when can has no suitable form: I’ll be able to come tomorrow, I want to be able to drive, I haven’t been able to sleep.

1a · Rewrite using be able to

Type the whole sentence. Small punctuation differences are ignored.

1My sister can’t walk because she has broken her leg.
2Can you lend me some money to go to a concert?
3I can drive but I haven’t got a car.
4We can see the sea from the window of our room.
5Can your boyfriend speak any foreign languages?
6I’m tired because I can’t sleep at night.

2 · Choose can / can’t where possible

If can is not possible, use the correct form of be able to.

1 I cook, but not as well as my mother.
2 I finish your book by the end of the week, I’m sorry.
3 My nephew play chess very well — he has won several competitions.
4 My grandparents use a computer. They have never learnt.
5 Oh no, it’s raining! We have a barbecue tonight.
6 We afford to go on a holiday this year, because we haven’t got enough money.

3 · Preparing for the future

Complete with can, can’t or the correct form of be able to.

Scientists say that there are many ways we 1 (keep) our brains healthy, so that we 2 (have) a normal life when we are older.

Learn a new activity. Think of something that you 3 (not do) but you would like to learn. Learning something new exercises your brain, so that you 4 (deal) better with new situations in the future.

Do some exercise. Doctors say that regular exercise might 5 (stop) the brain getting ill with Alzheimer’s. People who don’t exercise might have problems in later life because they 6 (sleep).

Have fun. Spending time with relatives 7 (make) you feel more positive. If you have friends, you 8 (phone) someone for a chat.

Listen to the silence. It is important to find a moment when you 9 (relax). This prepares us for the future, when we 10 (not go out) every day.

cancan’tbe able towill be able tocouldhave been able togood at + -ing

10 · Ability questions

1. What can you do now that you couldn’t do five years ago?
2. What would you most like to be able to do by this time next year?
3. What are you really good at doing? What are you not very good at?
4. Describe a difficult situation when you were able to solve a problem successfully.
5. What skills will people need to be able to use well in ten years?
6. Have you ever been unable to do something because technology failed?
7. Which abilities can people improve through practice, and which are harder to change?
8. What can you do to keep your brain active as you get older?

TARGETED ERROR CLINIC should — Stages 5–8

One rule worth making automatic: should + base verb. Say You should go, You shouldn’t worry, Should I call?. Never: should to go. The tasks below deliberately move from guided production to real-life use.

5) Направляемая речь · Guided speaking

TRY TO DO ORALLY FIRST. Read each situation and give advice. Start with the cue, but complete the idea yourself.

You should + verb You shouldn’t + verb I think you should + verb Maybe you should + verb
1. Your friend sleeps only five hours before an important exam.
Cue: I think you should…
Sample answer: I think you should go to bed earlier tonight and get at least seven or eight hours of sleep.
2. A student translates every English sentence word for word.
Cue: You shouldn’t…
Sample answer: You shouldn’t translate every sentence word for word. You should try to understand the general meaning first.
3. Someone wants to improve their speaking but never speaks outside lessons.
Cue: Maybe you should…
Sample answer: Maybe you should speak for ten minutes every day, even if you make mistakes.
4. Your colleague checks messages every two minutes and cannot concentrate.
Give one positive and one negative recommendation.
Sample answer: You should turn off non-essential notifications while you are working, and you shouldn’t check your phone every few minutes.
5. You are not sure whether to practise English when you are tired.
Ask for advice with Should I…?, then answer your own question.
Sample answer: Should I practise English when I’m tired? I think I should do a short, easy activity, but I shouldn’t force myself to study for hours.

6) Свободная речь · Free speaking

Speak for about 45–60 seconds on each question. No sentence beginnings are provided now. Use should / shouldn’t naturally at least twice.

1. What should adults do to keep their brains active as they get older?
Sample answer: Adults should keep learning new things and stay socially active. They should also exercise regularly, and they shouldn’t spend all day doing passive activities.
2. What should a language learner do when progress seems slow? What shouldn’t they do?
Sample answer: A language learner should focus on regular practice rather than immediate results. They should notice small improvements, and they shouldn’t compare themselves with advanced learners all the time.
3. Should schools teach memory techniques explicitly? Explain your view and give practical recommendations.
Sample answer: I think schools should teach a few practical memory techniques because students need to know how to learn efficiently. Teachers should show learners how to review material over time, but they shouldn’t present one method as a perfect solution for everyone.
01:00

7) Взаимодействие · Interaction

Discuss with ChatGPT, DeepSeek or a person.

The partner should challenge your advice or ask follow-up questions. Your job is to respond, clarify, and sometimes change your recommendation.

Role-play A · Learning problem
Your partner says: “I understand grammar exercises, but when I speak, I make the same mistakes.”
Give three pieces of advice. The partner should disagree with one of them. Defend or revise your advice.
Sample: You should practise the difficult structure in short spoken answers every day. You should also record yourself sometimes, but you shouldn’t correct every mistake while you are speaking.
Partner: Recording myself sounds uncomfortable.
You: That’s true, so perhaps you shouldn’t do it every day. You could start with one short recording a week.
Role-play B · Brain and concentration
Your partner says: “I study for four hours without breaks because breaks waste time.”
Ask two questions first. Then explain what they should and shouldn’t do.
Sample: How well can you concentrate during the last hour? Do you remember what you study afterwards? I think you should take short breaks every forty or fifty minutes. You shouldn’t spend the break scrolling through social media; you should stand up, walk around, or rest your eyes.
Role-play C · Advice exchange
Tell your partner about one real learning difficulty. Ask: “What do you think I should do?” After receiving advice, respond with That might work, but… or I’m not sure I should… because….
Sample: I keep forgetting new words after a few days. What do you think I should do?
Partner: You should review them every evening.
You: That might work, but I’m not sure I should review the entire list every day. Maybe I should choose ten words and recycle them in sentences.
Interaction notes
Sample answer: You should practise the structure in short spoken answers. You shouldn’t stop every time you make a mistake, because fluency also needs practice. I think you should record yourself sometimes and listen for repeated errors.

8) Перенос навыка · Transfer

Use should outside the exercise. This stage is deliberately personal and practical.

Mission 1 · Real recommendation. Think of a genuine problem you, a student, colleague, friend, or family member has. Write three recommendations you could actually say to them.
Sample answer: You should break the problem into smaller steps. You shouldn’t try to solve everything at once. I think you should ask someone for feedback after you have tried on your own.
Mission 2 · Real decision. Write one question you genuinely need advice about this week using Should I…?. Discuss it with a person or AI, then write the advice you received.
Sample answer: Should I spend more time reviewing old vocabulary this week? The advice I received was that I should review it briefly every day, but I shouldn’t stop learning new expressions completely.
Final automaticity check.
